core.title: Component URN casing: capability/feature kebab-lower, name facets kebab-lower or CamelCase
core.given: A component URN is involved, in any artifact
core.when: you write, copy or reference it
core.then: The product capability and feature segments must be kebab-lower, and each '.'-separated facet of the name segment must be kebab-lower or CamelCase; the name is a logical component name, written in PascalCase, camelCase, or dot-separated form.
avoid: A product capability or feature segment that is not kebab-lower.
core.why: Consistent casing lets the graph address components unambiguously and case-sensitively.
evidence: The product capability and feature segments match ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$.
The whole URN also matches the canonical component-URN pattern enforced by the companion URN-pattern rule.
verification: Checked wherever a component URN appears — in any artifact, whether newly written, edited, copied or referenced; copied or referenced URNs get no exemption, and an existing URN with invalid casing still fails.

The check applies the URN scheme's facet separator '.' inside the name segment, and the segment patterns: product capability and feature ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$; each name facet ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ (kebab-lower) or ^[A-Z][a-zA-Z0-9]*$ (CamelCase).

Where the stack's canonical component-URN pattern is inconsistent with these segment patterns (for example a character class that excludes '-' or lower-initial names), the inconsistency is recorded and not resolved here: every stated constraint stays mandatory and a URN must satisfy all of them; reconciliation requires a source-rule change.
The side and layer segments are fixed lower-case enumerations; their values are enforced by the companion URN-pattern rule, not by this casing check.
Observing the change activation fact needs a diff observer that extracts component-URN strings from a change and checks the segment casing patterns.

values: component URN string added, edited, copied or referenced

fires: A component URN appears in any artifact, whether new, edited, copied or referenced.

profileRequirements.meaning: The segment structure of the component URN — which segment is the product capability, the feature and the logical name, and their order and prefix — so the core's per-segment casing obligation binds to the right segments.

bunOnly.text: Source inconsistency, recorded and not resolved here: the lint regex name class [a-zA-Z0-9.]+ excludes '-', but kebab-lower facets (and 'lang-*' facets) contain '-'. The name description also allows camelCase, which the CamelCase facet regex ^[A-Z]... does not match. Every stated constraint stays mandatory; a URN must satisfy all of them. Reconciliation requires a source-rule change.

neutralityNotes: The casing obligation is the URN scheme's own lexical rule set — kebab-lower, CamelCase, camelCase and the '.' facet separator are identifier conventions that name no stack, runtime or language — so it stays in the core; the segment structure it binds to (component:{capability}:{feature}:{name}:{side}:{layer}) comes from the profile key urn.component, and no new vocabulary key was needed. Not neutralized: the concrete example/counter-example URNs, the pointer to the sibling pattern rule's id and evidence slot, and the concrete lint-regex inconsistency text (its generic policy — recorded, unresolved, every constraint mandatory — is in core.verification, and the camelCase-vs-CamelCase-facet-regex tension is preserved verbatim in bunOnly rather than resolved here). The bun activation-fact notes were folded into the core (observer scope in verification) rather than carried as extra fields.
